en: Virgin coconut oil is solid at cool room temperatures but melts into a clear liquid when heated for frying fish.
Abaca plant fibers possess high tensile strength and saltwater resistance, making them excellent natural materials for weaving marine ropes.
When you stir sugar and squeezed calamansi into water, they dissolve to form a homogeneous liquid mixture called a solution.
The reddish-brown rust forming on a corrugated iron roof during the rainy season is a chemical change creating iron oxide.
Steamed rice cakes like puto puff up because baking powder releases carbon dioxide gas that expands when heated.
Drying salted fish under the hot Philippine sun causes the liquid water inside the fish to evaporate into a gas.
A bowl of halo-halo is a heterogeneous mixture because you can easily see and separate its distinct solid ingredients.
Bamboo is a rapidly growing, lightweight, and highly flexible natural material traditionally used by Filipinos to build sturdy houses.
A green mango turning yellow and sweet on the branch undergoes a chemical change that alters its internal molecular structure.
Crushing a block of ice into smaller pieces for halo-halo is a physical change because the chemical composition of water remains unchanged.
Dried coconut husk fibers, called bunot, are highly abrasive physical materials traditionally used by Filipinos for scrubbing kitchen pots.
The sour taste of sinigang broth comes from tamarind acid dissolving in water to create a homogeneous aqueous solution.
